thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Poised To Retreat Slightly As Crucial Midterm Elections Get Under Way

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Poised To Retreat Slightly As Crucial Midterm Elections Get Under Way
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch
U.S. stock-index futures on Tuesday drifted lower, set for modest losses ahead of midterm elections that could set the political tone on Wall Street for at least the next two years.
How are the benchmarks performing?
Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average were off 38 points, or 0.2%, at 25,403, those for the S&P 500 index were off 5.60 points to reach 2,734, a decline of 0.2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.4%, down 26.50 points, at 6,923.
On Monday, the Dow rose 190.87 points to 25,461.70, a gain of 0.8%, and the S&P 500 added 15.25 points, or 0.6%, to end at 2,738.31. The Nasdaq Composite Index , meanwhile, fell 28.14 points, or 0.4%, to 7,328.85.
What's driving the market?
Midterm elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, are under way and the results could have implications for President Donald Trump's legislative agenda.
Check out:How traders are thinking about dollar wagers ahead of midterm elections, the Fed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-traders-are-thinking-about-dollar-wagers-ahead-of-midterm-elections-the-fed-2018-11-05)
In the final pre-election Wall Street Journal/NBC News poll released Sunday, Democrats held a 7 percentage-point lead on the question of which party should control the next Congress.
The most likely outcome of the elections is political gridlock, which has historically been a positive for investors, but may forestall expectations for infrastructure investments and further deregulation that might help lift shares of financial firms.
Meanwhile, investors were keeping one eye on crude-oil prices , a day after the Trump administration imposed fresh sanctions aimed at curtailing Iranian oil exports.
Abroad, market participants are also watching developments around U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May and her tense negotiations with the European Union to exit a longstanding pact with the trade bloc.
Read: Opinion: This is what's happened to stocks after every midterm election since World War II (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-whats-happened-to-stocks-after-every-midterm-election-since-world-war-ii-2018-11-05)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) were set to fall a third straight session after closing at its lowest level since Aug. 1 and booking its worst two-day decline since Jan. 25, 2013. Shares on Tuesday were off 0.5% in thin premarket action. Reports that the iPhone maker was scaling back on production of a new XR model phone contributed to its decline.
Shares of Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN) were in focus after reports that the retailing giant was set to pick two cities to host its second headquarters, possibly the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York and the Crystal City are of Arlington, Va., a Washington suburb. Shares of Amazon slipped 0.5% in premarket trade Tuesday.
Under Armour Inc.'s (UAA) stock rose 1.3% in premarket activity. A report in The Wall Street Journal said that employees received an email saying they were no longer able to expense strip-club outings (https://www.wsj.com/articles/under-armours-metoo-moment-no-more-strip-clubs-on-company-dime-1541450209).
Before the opening bell, quarterly reports from CVS Health Corp. (CVS), Eli Lilly & Co.(LLY), Archer Daniels Midland Co. (ADM) and Ralph Lauren Corp.(RL) are expected.

What data are in focus
A report on job openings for September due at 10 a.m. Eastern Time remains the only key data ahead on Tuesday.
What are analysts saying?
"Stocks still look to be able to rise further despite some minor stalling out over the past few days prior to this week's midterm elections. Looking back, yesterday proved that technology does not necessarily have to work every day for stocks to be able to log decent gains," said Mark Newton, founder of Newton Advisors in a Tuesday research note.
